# GEO report: quay-store

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 25 of 25 points).
How it's calculated: low = 12 ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. High = (12 + 0) ÷ 25 × 100 = 48. Both are capped at 40, because the code blocks Googlebot from the whole site (`static/robots.txt:5`). That is a blocker for GEO-009, which checks that search crawlers have the access you want.

Three things cost most of the points. Googlebot is told to stay out of the whole site. Pages are built in the browser instead of on the server. The root `<html>` tag has no language. The score is read from code, not measured on a live site. Nothing is left as "can't tell".

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. Your sitemap and canonicals use `quay.example`, which looks like a placeholder, so I don't know the real address.

## Do these first

### 1. Let Googlebot crawl the site
- **Why it matters:** Google is told not to crawl any page, so the site can't be found there, whatever else is fixed.
- **Where:** `static/robots.txt:4-5`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Googlebot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small (delete two lines)
- **Score after this:** 72/100. The 40 cap lifts, and GEO-009 and GEO-014 each earn 3 more points (12 → 18 of 25).

### 2. Send the page content in the server's HTML
- **Why it matters:** With `ssr = false`, the server sends an empty shell and the browser builds the page. Crawlers that don't run JavaScript see no text, headings or navigation links.
- **Where:** `src/routes/+layout.ts:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const ssr = false;`
- **Size:** Small to Medium. Remove the line, or prerender the pages. Check that nothing relies on browser-only APIs.
- **Score after this:** 84/100, after item 1 (21 of 25). GEO-003 earns 3 more points. On its own it stays at 40, because the cap stays while Googlebot is blocked.

### 3. Add `lang` and a description on every page
- **Why it matters:** The language tells machines how to read the text. `/shop` has an empty description and `/search` has none, so those pages have no summary.
- **Where:** `src/app.html:2`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` (also `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:3`: `<meta name="description" content="" />`)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 92/100, after items 1 and 2 (23 of 25). GEO-012 earns 2 more points.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and a sensible size | Clear | `static/robots.txt`. Plain text, valid lines. |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers get the access you want | Problem | `static/robots.txt:5` `Disallow: /` for Googlebot. This is a blocker. Bingbot falls under `*: Allow`. I assumed you want to be found, because there is no `geo.config.json`. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages can be indexed | Problem | `/` and `/shop` are both blocked for Googlebot by `robots.txt:5`. 0 of 2 routes clear. `/search` has a deliberate noindex and isn't in the sitemap. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | `/` and `/shop` have absolute canonicals on `quay.example`. `/search` is noindex. |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | `src/routes/+layout.ts:1` `export const ssr = false;`. No prerender setting and no `svelte.config.js` found. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD (structured data) is valid | Problem | `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5` is a Product with only `"name":"Bilge pump"`. Google's Product docs also require `offers`, `review` or `aggregateRating`. |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | `static/sitemap.xml` is valid, and `robots.txt:7` has an absolute `Sitemap:` line. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | `src/app.html:2` has no `lang`. `/shop` has an empty description and `/search` has none. |
| GEO-016 | Key pages are reachable through real links | Clear | `src/routes/+layout.svelte:5` has `<a href>` links to Home and Shop. |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`+layout.svelte:7`), which is a deliberate choice. No page-wide `nosnippet` or headers found. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | I read the layout and all 3 pages. There are no images, links have text, and every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | No app declared. |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | None present. |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | Not an app. |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

- **Replace the placeholder domain:** `static/sitemap.xml:3`: `<loc>https://quay.example/</loc>`. The same host is hardcoded in `robots.txt`, the sitemap and both canonicals. Swap in your real domain, ideally from one shared setting.
- **Make the Product data useful:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:5`: `"name":"Bilge pump"`. `/shop` lists a whole category rather than one product, so Product data on it may be the wrong type. Consider `ItemList`, or give each product its own page with price and availability.
- **Give each product its own page:** `+page.svelte:9`: `Bilge pumps, cleats and rope.` Each item could have a page and address that the shop and home page link to. Right now the home page only links to Shop.
- **Say what "next day" means:** `src/routes/+page.svelte:7`: `Marine parts, shipped next day`. Nothing states cutoff times, regions or cost as text. The "Free delivery over £50" line is deliberately hidden from snippets, so put the delivery details on a page of their own.
- **Add site identity data:** `+layout.svelte:5`. There is no Organization or WebSite JSON-LD with the store name and link, even though the name "Quay" appears in the home page title.
- **Make titles say who and what:** `src/routes/shop/+page.svelte:2`: `<title>Shop all parts</title>`. For example, "Shop all marine parts | Quay".
- **Add `lastmod` to the sitemap:** `static/sitemap.xml:3-4`. Neither URL has a date, and a date helps crawlers know when to re-read a page.
- **Add basic head and page structure:** `src/app.html:4` sets only `charset`, with no `viewport`. `+layout.svelte:6` has no `<main>` around `{@render children()}`.
- **Keep the sitemap in step with the pages:** `static/sitemap.xml` is hand-written. A generated sitemap would pick up new product pages automatically.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Live server behaviour:** real status codes and headers for `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and your pages. A live scan with your URL would settle these.
- **Prerendering at the host:** if your hosting prerenders pages, GEO-003 could change. Nothing in the repository shows that.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI tools to find this site. There is no `geo.config.json` to say otherwise.
- I read all 3 routes (`/`, `/shop`, `/search`), the layout, `app.html`, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and the single JSON-LD block. I found no `svelte.config.js`, `vite.config`, hooks, or `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
